solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A red line inside proofreading mark

definitions.note: a noun phrase: one red wine, a Bordeaux

indicators.note: the line is placed within the proofreading mark, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a caret is the wedge-shaped mark an editor uses to show where text is to be inserted

explanation.surface: A proofreader marks up a page, slipping a red line inside one of their insertion marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A red' reads like part of the description of the mark, but it is the definition: a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, so it is one example of a red.

clue.text: Senior relative in apartment, glaring

indicators.note: the relative is housed in the apartment, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a flat is the British word for an apartment
a gran, or grandmother, is an older relative

explanation.surface: An elderly relative living in a flat gives someone a glaring look.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something conspicuous and blatant, such as an obvious error or offence.

clue.text: Illuminated with it

definitions.meaning: lit up, as a lamp is when the power reaches it
informal for fashionable, alert and up to date

explanation.surface: Lit up, and in on the latest thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp turned on is lit; a person described this way is lively, aware and fashionable.

clue.text: Operatic star keen to come over

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over means turning the word end to end, so it is read backwards

parts.note: avid means eager or keen

explanation.surface: An opera singer is eager to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come over' looks like a visit, but it asks for AVID to be turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Quite rare, yet growing wild in former times

parts.note: 'Quite!' is an expression of agreement, like yes

indicators.note: plants growing wild are uncultivated and out of order, signalling a jumble of the letters

explanation.surface: Something once quite rare is now growing wild, unlike in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite' looks like a qualifier of 'rare', but it is the reply 'Quite!', meaning yes; 'growing wild' rearranges RARE YET into TERYEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means the past or bygone days; Collins also lists an adverbial use, in past times.

clue.text: Some overhead, but not this bird!

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are used, signalling a run hidden inside it

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes some birds flying overhead, but not this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that this bird cannot fly, so it will never be overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Bishop organised church's regional office

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run something is to organise it, so ran
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bishop set up a local office for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym, RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local outpost of a larger organisation, such as a bank's regional office.

clue.text: Exclamation from leader of pop band rejecting first love

indicators.note: the singer's name throws out one letter, signalling a deletion

parts.note: Boy George fronted the 1980s band Culture Club
love is zero in tennis, the letter O; the first such letter in the name is the one dropped

explanation.surface: A pop frontman cries out as he spurns his first sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY GEORGE has two Os; dropping the first gives the old oath.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British oath of surprise, invoking Saint George.

clue.text: Girl chess player, faultless

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
White is the side, or player, who moves first in chess

explanation.surface: A girl playing chess performs without a single mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally pure white like the flower, figuratively innocent and beyond reproach.

clue.text: Difficult years making one tough

parts.note: hard means difficult
Y is an abbreviation for year or years

explanation.surface: Hard years have made someone resilient.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy person or plant is robust and able to endure harsh conditions.

clue.text: Building a target for event held on water

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so the letters are put together in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is building a target for a contest staged on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, a sporting meeting staged on a river or sea.

clue.text: Apprentice in series, keen at heart

parts.note: a train of events is a series of them

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A trainee taking part in a series of courses is keen at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name someone learning a trade or job under supervision.

clue.text: Drink with group of players no end

indicators.note: with no end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A sports side has a drink together, seemingly without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the classic British hot drink, brewed from leaves.

clue.text: Shopkeeper's beard has her worried

definitions.note: read as 'shopkeeper is', the 's being the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: letters that are worried are pulled about and disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's facial hair has her anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A haberdasher sells sewing goods such as buttons, ribbons and thread; in the US, men's clothing.

clue.text: Disregard skirmish, notwithstanding

parts.note: a brush is a brief encounter or skirmish, as in a brush with the law
aside can mean apart from or notwithstanding, as in 'jokes aside'

explanation.surface: A minor clash is ignored regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something as unimportant is to ignore or disregard it.

clue.text: Welcome rise

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to be grateful for or value something
as a verb, to go up in value, as property or shares do

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is being thankful for something; the other is increasing in value over time.

clue.text: In Pontefract, Eddy appeared on stage

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie in the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy performed in a show in Pontefract, a town in West Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform a role in a play; the past tense covers having performed.

clue.text: A plea for help secures top fireproof material

indicators.note: the distress call holds the next piece fast within it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
best means top or finest

explanation.surface: A call for help locks in a top-quality fire-resistant material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used for fire-resistant insulation.

clue.text: Employ trick right away

indicators.note: the right is sent away, signalling that its letter is removed

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: Someone uses a trick straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately', but 'right' is R and 'away' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The two verbs are synonyms: to put something into service.

clue.text: Annoyance as card game curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two players using a 32-card pack

explanation.surface: A card game cut short leaves a player irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment from wounded pride.

clue.text: Question one, then hang traitor

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to sling is to hang or suspend something

explanation.surface: Interrogate someone, then hang the traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: From Vidkun Quisling, the Norwegian who collaborated with the Nazis, the word means a collaborating traitor.

clue.text: Don't declare amount to be paid for a crowd control measure?

parts.note: in cricket, a side that does not declare its innings closed will bat on
a charge is a fee or price

explanation.surface: Someone hides a sum owed, perhaps from customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declare' suggests tax or customs, but it is the cricket term for ending an innings early, the opposite of batting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton charge is police running at a crowd with truncheons to disperse it.

clue.text: Sailor needing to achieve objective

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to get something is to obtain or achieve it

explanation.surface: A seaman must reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is an aim or goal, the thing one is trying to reach.

clue.text: Dicky in trouble

definitions.meaning: British slang for weak or unwell, as in a dicky heart
badly off or in a bad way, as in faring badly

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe being in poor shape, whether in health or in fortune.

clue.text: Character wanting to hire over short period

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to let a property is to hire it out

indicators.note: a period that is short is cut before its end, so its final character is dropped

parts.note: a term is a period of time, such as a school term

explanation.surface: A person of character wants to hire someone for a short spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is a character of the alphabet, a single written symbol.

clue.text: Almost certain matter involves large balance

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: the matter wraps around the next piece, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: pus is matter produced by an infected wound
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: It is almost certain that the matter involves a large remaining sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an excess left over, as is a balance remaining after payments.

clue.text: Most important element

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, principal or ..., as in the main role
the heavy metal with symbol Pb

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is foremost or principal; the other is the soft grey metal, a chemical element.

clue.text: One of three allowed on outing

indicators.note: the second piece is put on, or after, the first

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
let means allowed

explanation.surface: One of three people is permitted to go on an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born to the same mother at one birth.

clue.text: Belch, perhaps, in play touring Belgium

definitions.note: Sir Toby Belch is a character in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

indicators.note: the play goes around the country, enclosing it

parts.note: to toy is to play with something
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A burp, perhaps, during a play on tour in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belch' looks like a burp, but it is Sir Toby Belch, so the answer is his first name; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Toby Belch, the carousing uncle in Twelfth Night, is one bearer of the name.

clue.text: Oxygen required by huge Greek character

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
mega means huge or enormous

explanation.surface: A huge Greek man needs oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Poet holding pipe recalled young lady coming out

indicators.note: the poet's name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tube is a pipe

explanation.surface: A poet with a pipe remembers a young woman making her entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives EBUT. 'Coming out' is the old society term for a young woman's formal introduction at a ball, not a disclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her first appearance in fashionable society, traditionally 'coming out'.
